intent: Make the robot more agile to fix slalom line loss on alternating bends while keeping the sensor array and wheel radius that already produce oval and s-bend completions. Mass 0.5 to 0.45 kg, body_length 0.12 to 0.10 m, wheel_track 0.12 to 0.115 m. Expect slalom max_error below 0.06 and slalom progress above 0.5, with oval and s-bend completions maintained.
learning: Iteration 4 showed that cutting yaw inertia and narrowing the track improved slalom progress (0.34 to 0.43) and reduced steering oscillation, so agility is the lever on alternating bends. Next iteration, check: (a) whether slalom max_error drops below 0.06, which would confirm the slalom is limited by turn response; (b) whether steering_oscillation rises above 0.3, which would mean the agility gain has outrun the damping and the track should return toward 0.12 m; (c) whether s-bend completions hold at or above 17/20; (d) whether oval completion_time stays near 1.75 s. Ask the Integrator whether kd or ki needs retuning after the mass and length reduction.
rationale: Iteration 4 is the best design so far (score 657.9). Oval completes 20/20 and s-bend 17/20, so the platform is working on those tracks. Slalom still fails in all 20 trials (off_track, progress 0.43, max_error 0.065). The iteration 3 to 4 change was the only one that moved slalom, and it moved it the right way. Progress rose from 0.34 to 0.43, steering_oscillation fell from 0.31 to 0.24 on the oval and from 0.22 to 0.24 on the slalom, and control_effort fell on the oval and slalom. Reducing mass, body length and track was therefore a net gain, not a trade-off. The slalom failure is loss of the line on alternating bends, which points to yaw response, not to speed or sensing (line_loss_events are about 1.35 and the sensors still see the tape). The off-track floor is 0.06 m at body_width 0.12 m, and widening the body does not help. This proposal continues the agility direction in a moderate step. Mass goes from 0.5 to 0.45 kg and body_length from 0.12 to 0.10 m, which lowers yaw inertia (mass*(L^2+W^2)/12) from about 0.0012 to about 0.0009, roughly 25% lower. wheel_track goes from 0.12 to 0.115 m, which adds turn authority per unit of wheel differential. Sensor layout (7 sensors, x = ±0.03 m, y = 0.08 m, 12 mm footprint), wheel_radius (0.04 m) and body_width (0.12 m) are unchanged, so the oval and s-bend completions carry over and the Integrator's controller work stays valid. Expected result: slalom max_error below 0.06, more slalom progress (target above 0.5), and s-bend completions held at or above 17/20. Risk: the more agile body may push steering_oscillation above 0.3, which would mean the Integrator needs more kd and I should return the track toward 0.12 m.
